content: For adults, the recommended dosage of cefixime is 400 mg per day. This can be administered as a single 400 mg tablet or capsule once daily, or the 400 mg tablet can be divided into two halves, with one half taken every 12 hours. For the treatment of uncomplicated cervical or urethral gonococcal infections, a single oral dose of 400 mg is advised. Both the capsule and tablet forms of cefixime can be taken with or without food. When treating infections caused by Streptococcus pyogenes, cefixime should be administered at a therapeutic dosage for a minimum duration of 10 days. For pediatric patients aged 6 months or older, the recommended dosage is 8 mg/kg/day of the oral suspension. This can be given as a single daily dose or divided into two doses of 4 mg/kg every 12 hours. It is important to note that a suggested dosage has been established for each pediatric weight range, and healthcare providers should refer to the appropriate dosing table. When prescribing a dose in milliliters, the concentration of the suspension must be specified, as cefixime (Suprax) oral suspension is available in three concentrations: 100 mg/5 mL, 200 mg/5 mL, and 500 mg/5 mL. Children who weigh more than 45 kg or are older than 12 years should receive the adult dosage. Chewable tablets of Suprax must be chewed or crushed before swallowing. For the treatment of otitis media, the chewable tablets or suspension should be used, as clinical trials have shown that these forms achieve higher peak blood levels compared to the tablet or capsule when administered at the same dose. Therefore, the tablet or capsule should not be substituted for the chewable tablets or suspension in the treatment of otitis media. In cases of infections caused by Streptococcus pyogenes, cefixime should be administered at a therapeutic dosage for at least 10 days. In patients with renal impairment, cefixime (Suprax) can be administered. For individuals with creatinine clearance levels of 60 mL/min or higher, the normal dosage and schedule can be used. For adults with reduced renal function, dose adjustments should be made according to the provided dosing table. It is important to note that neither hemodialysis nor peritoneal dialysis significantly removes cefixime from the body. For reconstitution of the oral suspension, once prepared, the suspension can be stored for up to 14 days at room temperature or under refrigeration without significant loss of potency. The bottle should be kept tightly closed, and the suspension should be shaken well before each use. Any unused portion of the suspension should be discarded after 14 days.
